title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your makerspace assistant has no code that saves anything between sessions. Yesterday a student finished a chat with it. Today the student opens a new chat and asks, "Did I finish my booking yesterday?" Which statement is correct?

options.text: It can answer, because the model keeps every earlier chat it has had
It cannot know, because the new context starts without yesterday's chat
It can answer, as long as the model's context window is big enough
It cannot know, because the booking system hides records from the model

items.stem: An agent's system prompt and tool descriptions take 2,000 tokens and the student's question takes 100. The model is called three times: the first call ends with a tool request of 50 tokens whose result is 400 tokens; the second ends with a tool request of 50 tokens whose result is 150 tokens; the third writes the final answer. The program re-sends the full history on every call. How many input tokens are sent in total across the three calls?
Your team must decide which saved information belongs in a database that the program controls, rather than in a free-form note that the model writes for itself. Which item belongs in the database?

options.text: That a student tends to prefer booking slots on weekends
That a student asked about filament types in a past chat
That a student likes short answers without extra detail
That a student passed the safety training for the band saw

items.stem: When manuals are split into chunks for search, a chunk reading "Set the speed to 40% and the power to 70%" is hard to retrieve correctly. In one sentence, what is the problem with this chunk?
A long session nears the context limit, so your program asks the model to summarize the conversation and starts a new context from that summary. What is the main risk of this step?

options.text: The summary may leave out a detail that matters later
The model loses its tools and cannot call them again
The summary can never be shorter than the original chat
The context window shrinks by the size of the summary
